question: What protection does Canada’s Public Servants Disclosure Protection Act give a federal public servant who makes a protected disclosure?
generated_answer: The Public Servants Disclosure Protection Act gives a federal public servant the right to disclose wrongdoing in the public sector to their supervisor or to the Public Sector Integrity Commissioner. You are protected against reprisal if you are acting in good faith and if the information is based on what is reasonable grounds to believe. The Public Servants Disclosure Protection Act also gives a public servant a right to seek the support of the Public Sector Integrity Commissioner if they believe they are the subject of reprisal. The Public Sector Integrity Commissioner may make recommendations to an employer on how to address a disclosure of wrongdoing or reprisal situation. The Public Servants Disclosure Protection Act also gives the Public Sector Integrity Commissioner the power to investigate disclosures of wrongdoing, including the power to summon witnesses and compel evidence. The Public Sector Integrity Commissioner reports to Parliament annually on the number and nature of disclosures of wrongdoing and reprisal complaints, as well as on any recommendations made to an employer. The Public Servants Disclosure Protection Act also gives the Public Sector Integrity Commissioner the power to make recommendations to the Treasury Board on how to improve the disclosure and protection regime.
